key_insight: Chemical gradients in porous and crowded media can drive colloids and droplets by diffusiophoresis and diffusioosmosis, strongly reshaping transport beyond classical dispersion and filtration.
engineering_relevance: Understanding and exploiting phoretic transport can improve filtration, soil remediation, microfluidic separation, and delivery in biological or soft porous materials.
method: Review the sources that generate and sustain solute gradients in porous media
Summarize the minimal physicochemical model for diffusiophoresis and diffusioosmosis
Compare experimental platforms and flow regimes, including dead-end pores and flowing pathways
evidence_signal: The abstract synthesizes recent experimental results showing enhanced removal from dead-end pores and order-of-magnitude changes in breakthrough and dispersion due to cross-streamline migration.
watch_item: Predictions may be highly sensitive to geometry, solute-gradient lifetime, and the transition from 2D algebraic mixing to 3D chaotic mixing.
paper_title: Diffusiophoretic transport of colloids and emulsions in complex environments
